thread.title: Close Update: Stocks Rally Back From Labor Market Report

title: Close Update: Stocks Rally Back From Labor Market Report
text:
Close Update: Stocks Rally Back From Labor Market Report May 04, 2018, 04:43:29 PM EDT By MT Newswires, MT Newswires Shutterstock photo
Wall Street's benchmark averages all closed significantly higher on Friday as investors applauded the April labor market report and its tame inflationary component, Warren Buffett's $131 million bet on Apple ( AAPL ), and remarks from Fed officials downplaying the central bank's fixation on price pressures.
With the help of technical support at their respective 200-day moving averages, the Dow and S&P 500 made an impressive comeback from their post-job report lows, but could not end the week in the green, while the Nasdaq ended the week with a 1.2% gain on strength in the technology sector.
Stocks were defensive before today's open as a result of the disappointing conclusion to trade talks between China and the US and ahead of the pivotal jobs report. Selling erupted when the below consensus 164,000 gain in non-farm payrolls and anemic wage growth overshadowed a 17-year low in the jobless rate.
As investors digested the "goldilocks" labor market report, stocks started to gain ground with the Nasdaq outperforming on a record high in Apple and strength in FAANG and semiconductors. The Dow and S&P poked into the green for the week on the back of statements from Fed presidents Dudley and Kaplan, but only the Nasdaq and Russell 2000 closed higher.
Related markets defied the risk-on trade that drove the Dow more than 300 points higher as gold was up nearly $3 per ounce, the dollar was unchanged against the yen but lower against the euro and British pound, and bond yields were flat to slightly higher.
